verdict.rationale: Flagsmith's Release Pipelines let users define stages with "triggers and actions" that advance flags automatically and can auto-generate change requests on promotion, so the product itself provides rule-driven automation. Its documented scope is limited to flag rollout stages, and the evidence does not say which events can act as triggers. Scheduled flags are one-off, time-based changes rather than event-triggered rules, and audit log webhooks only stream logs outward, so neither adds credit. missing for 10: documentation of supported trigger event types, general-purpose event→action rules beyond release stages, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Define stages that your flags progress through automatically, with triggers and actions that control rollouts to selected environments and audiences.
Release Pipelines can automatically generate change requests when promoting flags to production, eliminating manual effort and streamlining your deployment workflow.
Release Pipelines act as your intelligent release assistant, automating your entire feature flag deployment process.
